title: Polanus: saving grace is not anything created in us
source_text: IV. Quamvis autem Theologi Reformati agnoscant per Dei gratiam in scriptura sacra quandoque designari divini favoris & amoris erga nos munera & effecta, paucis tamen in locis gratiam eo sensu sumendam esse putant. Siquidem omnia illa loca ubi dicimur per Dei gratiam electi, vocati, justificati, servati, contendunt minime exponenda esse de dono aliquo nobis inhaerente, sed tantum de gratuito Dei amore & benevolentia. Uti praesertim apud Polanum videre est. Gratia, inquit, Deo gratum atque acceptum faciens, atque ita & gratia salvans, qua sumus electi in Christo ad salutem aeternam, efficaciter vocati, justificati, regenerati, qua denique aeternum servamur, non est qualitas nobis infusa, non aliquid in nobis creatum & inhaerens, non charitas qua nos Deum diligimus, aut ulla alia virtus in nobis. Syntagmatis Theologici lib. 2. cap. 21. modo citato.
pass_a_gloss: IV. But although Reformed Theologians acknowledge that by the grace of God in sacred scripture are sometimes designated the gifts and effects of divine favour and love toward us, yet they think that in few places grace is to be taken in that sense. Since they contend that all those places where we are said to be by the grace of God elected, called, justified, saved, are by no means to be expounded of some gift inhering in us, but only of the free love and benevolence of God. As especially is to be seen in Polanus. Grace, he says, making pleasing and accepted to God, and so also saving grace, by which we are elected in Christ to eternal salvation, efficaciously called, justified, regenerated, by which finally we are eternally saved, is not a quality infused into us, not something created and inhering in us, not the charity by which we love God, or any other virtue in us. Syntagma Theologicum book 2. chap. 21. just cited.
pass_b_english: Thesis IV. The Reformed theologians do grant that in holy scripture the grace of God sometimes means the gifts and effects of God's favour and love toward us. Still, they think grace is to be taken that way in only a few places.

For they hold that every passage saying we are chosen, called, justified or saved by God's grace must not be explained of some gift that inheres in us. These passages refer only to God's free love and goodwill. This can be seen especially in Polanus.

Grace that makes us pleasing and acceptable to God, he writes, and so saving grace as well, by which we are chosen in Christ for eternal salvation, effectually called, justified and regenerated, and by which in the end we are saved forever, is not a quality infused into us. It is not something created and inhering in us, not the love with which we love God, nor any other virtue in us (Syntagma, book 2, chapter 21, cited just above).

choices.english: grace freely given ... grace that makes pleasing
choices.why: The scholastic pair (Aquinas, Summa theologiae I-II q. 111 a. 1): gifts given for the good of others versus the grace that makes its bearer pleasing to God. Kept literal because the Reformed objections turn on the very words.
